## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle update (loop1) can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads, with the optimized render pass (loop2) adding bounded overhead.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.0, cost FALLS from 3.381 ns/p at N=4000 to 3.001 ns/p at N=262000 — overhead amortization across the measured range, with no visible knee at the L1d spill (N≈963, below all sampled points). The L2 spill at N≈61680 falls between N=16000 (3.255) and N=65000 (3.056); cost continues to improve through it, then RISES mildly to 3.134 at N=1000000 and 3.227 at N=4000000 — a soft DRAM-floor penalty, not a sharp knee. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the N-curve: at q=0.25 the curve is essentially FLAT from N=16000 onward (7.892→7.934 ns/p), and at q=0.5 it is FLAT across all N (27.3±0.3 ns/p), indicating the respawn path dominates cost entirely and cache residency is irrelevant.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 22.66 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.0 — 89.8% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algorithm is bandwidth-bound at q=0.0 across all N≥16000. It transitions to overhead-bound immediately upon introducing death: q=0.01 already drops to 13.48 GB/s (53%), q=0.25 to 8.52 GB/s (34%), and q=0.5 collapses to 2.48 GB/s (10%). The q=0.75 point recovers partially to 5.94 GB/s, suggesting the q=0.5 regime hits a pathological respawn-churn path. The hypothesis of approaching the streaming ceiling holds only at q=0.0; any nonzero death rate pushes the algorithm far below ceiling.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. `fmul.4s v0, v3, v4` and `fadd.4s v0, v1, v0` operate on four float lanes of a single particle's position; `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc` rearranges bytes to assemble the 4-lane operand, and `mov.s v3[3], v0[0]` inserts the scalar result. A gather appears as `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` — a single indexed element load for one component. The render phase uses `uqadd.8b v5, v5, v4` for byte-granular saturating adds, but the 16 `strb` and 13 `ldrb` instructions reveal byte-granular scatter writes that cannot stream. PMC at q=0.0 shows 60% useful, 22% processing, 17.9% discarded — the discarded cycles likely reflect the byte-store scatter and the `bl _layouts.ML1.data.Data.spawn` call path, consistent with bandwidth capping at 90% rather than 100%.

## Verdict
Partially holds — at q=0.0 the algorithm sustains 22.66 GB/s = 89.8% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling with no cache-spill knee, confirming autovec approaches streaming on death-free workloads. But any nonzero death rate collapses it: q=0.01 drops to 13.48 GB/s (53%) and q=0.5 to 2.48 GB/s (10%), because the branchy respawn path (`udiv`, `msub`, `bl spawn`) and byte-granular render scatter dominate. The hypothesis holds only in the death-free regime.
